description: Cattle Heat Stress Information is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USDA Agricultural Research Service; National Weather Service. Heat stress for cattle is based on temperature, humidity, wind speed, and cloud cover. This site offers information on recognizing heat stress in animals and options for taking action to minimize heat stress before and during an extreme heat event. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Extreme Heat. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Economy. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
